main_body: marble column with capital, shaft, and base
top_band: light grey/white top surface of the capital at rows 9-12 (4 rows tall, bounded by row 8 back outline and row 12 bright white front-edge highlight)
evidence: Reading down the middle column: row 8 is the top back outline; rows 9-11 are the light grey top plane of the capital; row 12 is a bright white 1px front-edge highlight line; rows 13-15 are the shaded front vertical rim of the capital; row 16 is the dark eave/neck shadow directly beneath the capital overhanging the shaft (rows 17-39) and base (rows 40-46). However, notice that the capital (rows 9-15) and the base (rows 41-46) are nearly identical horizontal banded shapes (3 rows light, 1 row white band, 2 rows grey), which makes the capital read somewhat ambiguously like a front-elevation molded torus rather than a clear elliptical/planar top surface as in the guide.

style.evidence: The column uses a 6-step cool grey/white ramp with dark grey-purple outlines (dark material tone) and vertical cylindrical shading plus subtle stone grain/mottling along the shaft. Compared to the Beodeul props, it is clean and well-shaded for a smooth marble pillar, though simpler in surface detail.
